decision: SCOPE + DIFFERS -> W3 accept (umd_ext growing-peppers names 'Habanero types' in its ripening text; it is the closest-scoped pepper page) and W1. UMD states "Spacing: 12"- 24" in-rows x 30"- 36" between row" -> in_row [12,24], row [30,36]. Today's [18,24] is on no cited pepper page (UMN/USU/ISU 18; UGA and VCE 12-24; Clemson 12); the NCSU capsicum-chinense toolbox field is a footprint. Prose restating 18-24 is re-authored to 12-24 (and its rows 24-36 to UMD's 30-36).

edits.new: Harden the plants off over about a week, then plant them about 12 to 24 inches apart into warm soil. A sheet of black plastic mulch warms the soil and helps, and a collar around each plant keeps cutworms off.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (UMD: 12-24 in)

edits.new: Harden off over 7 to 10 days, then transplant into warm soil, about 12 to 24 inches apart in rows 30 to 36 inches apart. On heavy or cool soil, black plastic or fabric mulch warms the ground and gives the crop a head start. A cutworm collar protects each new transplant.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row and row figures (UMD: 12-24 in, rows 30-36 in)

restatements.note: a quantity per foot of row (fertilizer or yield), not a plant-spacing restatement
